modified. It provides real Cogent offscreen widget routing and software composition;
it does not yet provide the public managed Vellum replay driver or complete P9.

## Checked API

```go
// Requires an offscreen process selected at build/startup, before any window.
func (*core.Stage) RunManual(context.Context, core.ManualWindowConfig) (*core.ManualWindow, error)

type ManualWindowConfig struct {
    Size image.Point
    LogicalDPI float32
    EventCapacity int
    Now func() time.Time
    NewShaper func() (shaped.Shaper, error)
    AfterFunc func(context.Context, time.Duration, func()) (core.ManualTimer, error)
}
type ManualTimer interface { Stop() bool }

func (*core.ManualWindow) Input(context.Context, core.ManualInput) error
func (*core.ManualWindow) Step(context.Context, int) (core.ManualStepResult, error)
func (*core.ManualWindow) Frame(context.Context) (core.ManualStepResult, error)
func (*core.ManualWindow) Image(context.Context) (*image.RGBA, error)
func (*core.ManualWindow) Snapshot(context.Context) (core.ManualSnapshot, error)
func (*core.ManualWindow) Close(context.Context) error
```

`ManualInput` contains event Type, Rune, Code, Modifiers, Button, Position and
scroll Delta. Supported primitives are key down/up/chord, pointer down/up/move,
and scroll. Admission validates primitives and checks capacity before Source
mutation. It does not itself validate managed control IDs, incarnations or model
revisions; those belong in the public driver adapter.

`Snapshot` reports Now, queued Events, reserved-head Blocked, ReadyPaint,
FuturePaint/NextPaint, frame-pass count, Closed, Failure and admitted Timers.
`Step(maximum)` performs at most that many actual originating Deque dispatches;
it does not advance time. Exhausting a positive batch is a normal bounded return,
so the outer runner must account MaxSteps and inspect residual work. Zero/negative
budget refuses. `Frame` requests paint and performs one real next dispatch using
the existing Front priority; callers inspect the returned type and/or step until
the requested paint has routed. `Frames` counts routed WindowPaint passes, not a
promise that every pass recomposed unchanged pixels. `Image` returns detached
software pixels and refuses before a frame.

The checked execution adapter can directly wrap `ManualClock.Now` and
`AfterFunc` (its Timer structurally implements Stop). Capture clock readiness
separately: core Timers counts armed/queued/running origin credits; it does not
contain due/future deadlines. `ReadySnapshot.CurrentIdle` distinguishes future
armed clocks from current-instant ready work. The runner never implicitly
advances the clock to a deadline.

## Ownership and production compatibility

Manual construction selects both loop suppressions before window publication:
no offscreen WinLoop and no renderWindow eventLoop; no hidden first render.
Actual `renderWindow.handleEvent` routes stages/modal/disabled/hit testing/focus,
then the Scene EventBoundary. Software painting uses the real update/style/
layout/gather/compose/deferred path. Public adapter callbacks must execute outside
`Application.Do`, because existing widgets enter that owner themselves. Preserve
the originating Custom handler and OrderedPump path, rather than pre-draining
messages or invoking Change/Activate directly.

The `offscreen` build tag now excludes desktop driver initialization. The final
actual `go list` records prove exclusive selection in offscreen and default modes.
No runtime global driver replacement is supported. Construction rejects mixed
manual/automatic windows, non-offscreen drivers, asynchronous system-window
creation and a prepublication timer admission. Every independent system window
must be constructed explicitly through RunManual. Same-window dialogs/popups
inherit the manual context, clock and explicit shaper.

Nil/default production clocks keep original wall time and loops. Manual Sources
and newly generated widget events receive the selected clock; cloned events
preserve their original admitted timestamp. Explicit per-window viewport/DPI and
embedded `fonts.Default` shapers eliminate ambient font selection in this fixture.
Theme/palette and global timing preferences still require an explicit fixture
configuration in the public adapter. There is no cross-host GPU pixel promise.

## Timer and lifetime scope

Actual long-hover/press/repeated-click callbacks use checked bounded scheduling.
Due Clock callbacks only enqueue immutable origin events; actual widget mutation
happens in Step. Timer credit survives queued cancellation until dispatch/unlink,
so repeated fire/Stop cannot accumulate unlimited tombstones. Scene/window
retirement cancels deadlines. Manual paint deadlines, scroll focus/auto-scroll,
animation elapsed time and field undo grouping use the injected clock.

Completion delays and popup/snackbar timeouts currently refuse with an explicit
terminal unsupported-timer error; they never fall back to wall scheduling in
manual mode. Widget-specific textcore/cursor timers remain a later integration
gate. User callbacks cannot be killed by Go: cancellation may stop later work,
but a currently running callback owns the operation until it actually returns.
Concurrent/reentrant and copied controller calls refuse. Callback panic/Goexit
is terminal; panic-value formatting never runs arbitrary user String/Error code.
A normal close request evaluates a detached live stage/scene identity snapshot
from topmost scene to main. A topmost dialog veto preserves the underlying main
and native window; accepted scenes are destructively closed once. This does not
make all-scene vetoes transactional: a later veto cannot undo an earlier accepted
scene close. Force Close retires the controller, native software window, render
registry, queues and timers after a fault. Arbitrary widget Destroy panic can still stop
later sibling Destroy callbacks in stock tree cleanup; complete arbitrary
resource cleanup is not claimed.

## Next integration checkpoint

Root owns the public managed driver wrapper and bounded replay Record/Runner.
Use stable registration order, explicit window/control incarnation checks and
actual pointer/key routing for the project-property/table/task/history fixture.
Construct the existing managed records in a Body, then call its Stage.RunManual;
retain Body/Stage handles for actual geometry and focus capture. Do not use the
ordinary driver Run or Body.AssertRender, because those start hidden loops.
Run identical immutable records at event batches 1, 7 and 64. Compare actual
managed semantic state, domain/history/tasks, focused control/selection, rendered
layout rectangles and the controlled software image. Preserve origin reservations
and EventBoundary ordering and bound feedback with explicit MaxSteps. The current
core fixtures prove routing and timers, not that managed public workload yet.

Remaining P9 gates are that public wrapper, three authoritative workloads and
all workload-relevant timers. Cocoa input, external AX, native services and GPU
acceptance remain separate existing target-runtime proofs, not virtualized here.

# Stage31 owned timer checkpoint (temporary only)

This delta applies on the approved native-v2 stage30. It qualifies real Cogent offscreen event routing and software rendering. It does not virtualize Cocoa input, Accessibility, native services or GPU timing, and it is not the complete P9 application replay acceptance.

## Checked contracts

- `ManualWindow.RequestFrame(ctx) error` validates the same controller/self/context/lifetime/failure admission as other manual methods, coalesces a native paint request and dispatches no event. Explicit `Step` owns event/frame budget. `Frame` remains the existing request-and-one-step convenience.
- `Scene.ManualExecution`, `ManualAfterFunc` and `ManualFailure` expose the existing checked origin timer transport for TextCore. The clock callback only enqueues a DeferredEvent; widget/parser work runs in Step, behind prior ordinary input. Capacity includes canceled queued nodes until dispatch/unlink.
- Completion delay and reset/cancel use that transport in manual scenes. `Complete.SetWaitDuration` supplies a per-instance delay without mutating timing settings. Default scenes retain real scheduling. Snackbar/popup expiry uses its actual scene origin/lifetime.
- Cursor timestamps use the scene clock. Manual scene cursor ownership avoids the ambient global last-cursor references; explicit paint deadlines drive offscreen cursor frames. Ordinary offscreen/native cursor policy remains the default.
- `Lines.BindManualExecution(view, config)` validates a single live view, immutable execution lease and no pending/running ambient markup/autosave/reader. There is no implicit adoption or cross-scene clock rebinding. TextCore binds before style/highlighting; SetLines and Destroy cancel and release the lease.
- Actual markup debounce (500ms) and zero-delay explicit ReMarkup execute through the origin transport. Advancing the clock only admits work; it cannot parse, render or call widget listeners. Edit/region/Lines-generated event timestamps use the bound clock.
- `Lines.BeginAmbientWork` reserves default worker lifetime before it starts. Manual mode records and returns `ErrManualAmbient`; OutputBuffer refuses before reading or allocating its batch. Autosave toggled after binding refuses the worker before file access, while the preceding text edit stays accepted. Reader batching deadlines remain real in default mode; pending EOF timers are canceled and stale callbacks are sealed before worker release.

## Acceptance scope

Core fixtures exercise actual completion popup creation, reset/queued cancellation, snackbar expiry/early retirement, exact-deadline cursor image changes, enqueue-only frame admission and callback terminalization. TextCore fixtures use embedded licensed fonts, an exact CRLF/Unicode document, real pointer/key routing and real JSON highlighter markup. They check explicit delay/step separation, debounce supersession, buffer replacement, cursor focus, conflicting views, parser listener panic/Goexit unwind and unsupported reader refusal. Lines fixtures check lease identity, pending/running/autosave/shared-view adoption, nil/typed-nil/error timer refusal, worker lifetime and after-adoption autosave refusal. Watchdog deadlines bound deadlock failures; they do not advance virtual time.

OutputBuffer reader batching and filesystem autosave are explicitly unsupported manual features, not clocked support. Arbitrary widget Destroy panic may stop later sibling resource callbacks, as already recorded for stage30. The public managed wrapper and three authoritative P9 workloads need independent integration proof. Timing settings, font preferences, system input sources and Accessibility settings are unchanged.

// ManualFont is checked, detached font data. Name is a slash-separated local

// ManualInput either supplies physical coordinates or resolves a current target

	Window            string

	Target            string
	TargetIncarnation uint64
	Type              events.Types
	Rune              rune
	Code              key.Codes
	Modifiers         key.Modifiers

}

type ManualElement struct {
	ID, Parent                          string

	Enabled, Focused, Visible, Selected bool

}
type ManualWindowSnapshot struct {
	ID                                                      string
	Incarnation                                             uint64

}

	Application app.PendingState
	Clock       execution.ClockReadiness

}
type ManualStepResult struct{ Events, OwnerCallbacks, Frames int }

// Manual owns actual offscreen managed windows. Methods have one dispatch
// owner and refuse concurrency/reentrancy; callbacks may call Application APIs,
// but must not call back into this adapter. Clock and executor remain caller
// owned and are never implicitly advanced/stepped/closed.
type Manual struct {
	self           *Manual
	busy           atomic.Bool
	closed         atomic.Bool
	implementation *manualImplementation
}

# Managed manual adapter candidate

This temporary candidate adds public `cogent.NewManual` and is not installed in canonical Vellum. Its supported backend is Cogent's actual offscreen driver with the reviewed stage30 manual foundation and stage31 checked timer/RequestFrame overlay. Desktop builds refuse construction before creating a window. It qualifies software widget routing and composition, not macOS Cocoa input, GPU rendering, OS accessibility, human IME, or performance.

`cogent/` copies the committed native adapter and adds only `manual.go`, `manual_offscreen.go`, `manual_desktop.go`, and self-contained driver tests. `vellum/` and `consumer/` are frozen copied dependencies. `qualification/` is a separate consumer module importing only the public adapter; the driver module has no example dependency.

## Contract

The caller supplies an open `app.Application`, a checked `execution.ManualClock`, a bounded `execution.Manual`, checked font bytes plus SHA256 names, explicit managed colors/typography, and event/owner/window capacities. Fonts are parsed and copied before layout; the shaper reads only the supplied in-memory font FS. The first checkpoint shares one clock across registered driver windows. The application domain and fixture commands belong to its owner; caller code must not mutate widgets or advance the clock concurrently with adapter methods.

This checkpoint allows one active managed Manual application per process, with multiple independent registered windows. Another application refuses before widget/native construction; the process reservation retires on returned error, panic/Goexit rollback, or completed Close. The adapter owns the application's registered native windows and sole wake handler. Construction performs controlled reconciliation but no queue drain, frame, worker step, or virtual-time advance. A construction error retires partial/mounted native resources and restores dirty registration without force-closing a previously open domain. Owner `View` panic or `runtime.Goexit` retains normal Go unwinding and the application's fail-closed owner behavior, while deferred rollback attempts every native retirement and releases the adapter claim.

All adapter methods check the exact adapter identity and refuse concurrent/reentrant dispatch. Descriptor callbacks must return normally; they may use public application APIs but cannot reenter the manual adapter. Clock and executor remain caller-owned; accepted jobs survive cancellation/adapter close until the caller explicitly steps their terminal cleanup.

`Input` admits actual keys and physical pointer primitives to the originating Core Source. Optional window/control incarnation checks resolve a measured target to its actual pixel center; this does not invoke descriptor callbacks. Keys always follow Core's actual focused widget. Raw coordinates deliberately bypass target convenience checks so qualification proves actual modal and disabled routing. Closed domain windows refuse input/capture/frame admission before native topology retirement. No domain ID can be reopened.

`Step(ctx, maximum)` spends at most `maximum` combined originating events and owner mailbox callbacks, using fixed window registration order and bounded owner drain quanta. Frames count a subset of events. One Custom dispatch may drain only its remaining owner budget; arrivals posted by it remain for a later explicit batch. This is the existing app `DrainN` arrival cutoff, not a placeholder queue. No selected Manual job or clock timer is implicitly executed or advanced.

`RequestFrame` only requests paint and performs no reconciliation, event dispatch, owner work, layout or virtual advance. Later `Step` charges the work. `Frame` is a convenience that requests paint and processes one originating node plus at most `OwnerBatch` owner callbacks; an earlier Front node may win and `Frames==0` means no capture. Replay budgets should use RequestFrame + Step.

`Snapshot` reports detached last-frame measured geometry, semantic values, actual focus and UTF16 selection, plus current owner/executor/clock and originating event/paint/timer readiness. Dirty or queued work marks layout pending; canceled domain/native retirement is explicit. Due timers and future timers are distinct. Future-only timers and future paint do not require implicit advance. A capture refuses stale/pending queue or layout state; it never inserts a frame. Successful `Capture` returns copied software RGBA pixels. It does not prove a particular frame changed pixels when Core correctly reused unchanged composition.

`Close` explicitly force-closes the application domain, revokes queued window results, disposes managed control/editor bindings and retires every owned native window. It does not prompt a close policy, step accepted Manual workers, close the caller's executor/clock, or join arbitrary caller goroutines. Context-refused close performs no mutation; a partial cleanup remains retryable. Snapshot remains available for terminal accounting.

Unsupported extensions (including GPU/workbench extensions), OS file-drop service descriptors, native application menu/chooser/clipboard services, all configured clipboard chords, non-left context-menu pointer input, and Core manager screenshot/zoom/refresh/search/menu/window-focus shortcuts refuse before reconciliation or event admission. These unqualified fallback commands can write files/settings, render outside explicit frame accounting, or create unmanaged global UI. The retained managed dialog, command shortcut, focus navigation and controlled field behaviors use the same production controllers. No Cocoa attachment/main-queue publication worker is started; ordinary legacy multiline keyboard synchronization can use its originating event boundary, but native SettleEditor/IME/AX APIs are outside this offscreen checkpoint.

Control count is bounded before allocation (`MaxControls`, default 4096, maximum 65536), hierarchy by public UI validation, fonts by 32 files/4 MiB each/16 MiB total, window pixels by Core's checked 16M-pixel bound, and queued input by each originating event capacity. Budgets count discrete work, not callback CPU time; a blocking user callback remains caller work and cannot be preempted.

## Qualification scope

The independent public consumer declares a project, controlled property field and history, virtual table projection, tasks and same-window modal. Tests drive real routed pointer/key input, with no direct Change/Activate calls. They cover open, property edit, sorting/row selection, canceled selected worker completion, Undo, disabled raw hits/keys, modal raw background interception/Escape, control remount/refocus/stale target refusal, immutable software capture and terminal closure. Batch 1/7/64 compares exact domain state and actual measured elements/focus/selection/image; frame/event counts may differ and are reported separately. Driver units cover font/config/identity/refusal, construction panic/Goexit cleanup, domain-close capture guards, registration order/independent windows, full ordinary queue with reserved result delivery, future timer originating dispatch, and enqueue-only frame budgets.

This proof is scoped to the supplied fonts, declared theme, pinned Core/typesetting sources and software backend. It makes no cross-OS image equivalence, global pixel-golden, long-running scheduling fairness or UI replay transport claim. Root's replay runner/record integration is a separately reviewed consumer.

    for path in [Path("/private/tmp/vellum-p9-native/qualification-v2.json"), Path("/private/tmp/vellum-p9-timers/qualification-v2.json")]:
        data[str(path)] = sha(path)
    return data


def run(spec):
    name, directory, args = spec
    log = OUT / (name + ".log")
    command = ["go", *args]
    start = time.monotonic()
    with log.open("wb") as handle:
        handle.write((json.dumps({"command": command, "cwd": str(ROOT / directory)}) + "\n").encode())
        handle.flush()
        try:
            completed = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT / directory, stdout=handle, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=180)
            code = completed.returncode
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            handle.write(b"QUALIFICATION PROCESS TIMEOUT\n")
            code = 124
    return {"name": name, "command": command, "cwd": str(ROOT / directory), "exit_code": code, "elapsed_seconds": round(time.monotonic() - start, 3), "log": str(log), "log_sha256": sha(log)}

    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    before = inputs()
    compiler = subprocess.check_output(["go", "version"], text=True).strip()
    flags = ["-mod=readonly", "-tags", "offscreen", "-overlay", str(OVERLAY)]
    specs = [
        ("driver-race20", "cogent", ["test", *flags, "-race", "-count=20", "-timeout=120s", "-v", "./..."]),
        ("consumer-race3", "qualification", ["test", *flags, "-race", "-count=3", "-timeout=120s", "-v", "./..."]),
        ("driver-vet", "cogent", ["vet", *flags, "./..."]),
        ("consumer-vet", "qualification", ["vet", *flags, "./..."]),
        ("desktop-refusal", "cogent", ["test", "-mod=readonly", "-race", "-count=1", "-run", "^TestManualDesktopRefusesBeforeConstruction$", "-v", "./..."]),
    ]
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as pool:
        checks = list(pool.map(run, specs))
    build = run(("consumer-build", "qualification", ["test", *flags, "-race", "-c", "-o", str(OUT / "managed-qualification.test")]))
    checks.append(build)
    after = inputs()
    changed = {path: [value, after.get(path)] for path, value in before.items() if after.get(path) != value}
    changed.update({path: [None, value] for path, value in after.items() if path not in before})
    report = {
        "result": "PASS" if not changed and all(check["exit_code"] == 0 for check in checks) else "FAIL",
        "scope": "temporary public managed offscreen input routing and software composition; no GUI, Cocoa, OS AX, GPU or performance qualification",
        "compiler": compiler, "inputs": before, "input_count": len(before), "changed_inputs": changed, "checks": checks,
        "binary": {"path": str(OUT / "managed-qualification.test"), "sha256": sha(OUT / "managed-qualification.test")} if build["exit_code"] == 0 else None,
        "limits": ["one active managed application per process with multiple windows and one shared explicit clock", "future timers/jobs never execute implicitly", "caller callbacks must return normally; work budgets are not CPU-time budgets", "legacy offscreen keyboard origin only; no native SettleEditor/IME attachment", "software images are scoped to pinned inputs and supplied fonts/theme"],
    }
    path = OUT / "qualification.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps({"result": report["result"], "proof": str(path), "proof_sha256": sha(path), "input_count": len(before), "checks": [{"name": item["name"], "exit_code": item["exit_code"], "elapsed_seconds": item["elapsed_seconds"]} for item in checks], "changed_count": len(changed)}, indent=2), flush=True)
    raise SystemExit(0 if report["result"] == "PASS" else 1)

    main()

# Additional caller ownership contract

This supplements the frozen managed candidate README and v2 qualification proof. It changes no runtime input or measured result.

The caller must keep Cogent global settings, palette, keymap and highlighting configuration fixed while a managed Manual application exists. The explicit Vellum theme overlays pinned Cogent bootstrap defaults; it does not reset every global material/style/timing setting. Offscreen bootstrap uses its temporary data directory rather than loading a user's desktop preference files. One active managed application per process, plus refusal of unqualified manager shortcuts, bounds the supported dispatch owner; it does not authorize unrelated caller code to mutate those globals.

`ManualConfig.Executor` is a borrowed readiness handle. Construction does not replace executors in task or document managers that the domain has already created. The caller must inject that same executor explicitly through `tasks.NewWithConfig` or `document.Config.Executor` for workers whose readiness the adapter should report. The supplied consumer does so. Other caller goroutines and workers remain outside this checkpoint's deterministic accounting.

The shared clock, executor and global configuration are immutable dependencies during an adapter operation. The caller may explicitly advance the clock or step selected workers between operations; adapter construction, Input, RequestFrame, Step, Frame, Snapshot and Capture never perform those steps implicitly.

package cogent

import (
	"errors"
	"image"

	"time"

	"github.com/dshills/vellum/ui"
)

var (
	ErrManualConfig      = errors.New("cogent: invalid manual configuration or copied adapter")
	ErrManualUnsupported = errors.New("cogent: manual routing requires the offscreen driver")
	ErrManualBusy        = errors.New("cogent: concurrent or reentrant manual operation")
	ErrManualClosed      = errors.New("cogent: manual adapter or window closed")
	ErrManualStale       = errors.New("cogent: stale manual window or control incarnation")
	ErrManualLayout      = errors.New("cogent: target requires a current explicit frame")
	ErrManualDisabled    = errors.New("cogent: target is disabled or hidden by a modal")
)

// ManualFont is checked, detached font data. Name is a slash-separated local
// font filename; the digest is required. No ambient system font lookup occurs.
type ManualFont struct {
	Name, SHA256 string
	Data         []byte
}
type ManualConfig struct {
	Clock                                 *execution.ManualClock
	Executor                              *execution.Manual
	Fonts                                 []ManualFont
	Theme                                 ui.Theme
	Commands                              *command.Registry
	LogicalDPI                            float32
	EventCapacity, OwnerBatch, MaxWindows int
	MaxControls                           int // zero uses 4096; each window descriptor is checked before allocation.
}

// ManualInput either supplies physical coordinates or resolves a current target
// to its measured center. Keys still route through actual focus; targets never
// invoke a descriptor callback. Window incarnation is always required.
type ManualInput struct {
	Window            string
	WindowIncarnation uint64
	Target            string
	TargetIncarnation uint64
	Type              events.Types
	Rune              rune
	Code              key.Codes
	Modifiers         key.Modifiers
	Button            events.Buttons
	Position          image.Point
	Delta             math32.Vector2
}

type ManualElement struct {
	ID, Parent                          string
	Incarnation                         uint64
	Kind                                ui.Kind
	Name                                string
	Value                               any
	Enabled, Focused, Visible, Selected bool
	Selection                           [2]int // UTF-16 range; focus direction is preserved separately.
	TextFocus                           int
	Bounds                              image.Rectangle // actual scene pixels, including dialog scene origin.
}
type ManualWindowSnapshot struct {
	ID                                                      string
	Incarnation                                             uint64
	Elements                                                []ManualElement
	FocusedID                                               string
	Frames                                                  uint64
	Now, NextPaint                                          time.Time
	Events, Timers                                          int
	Blocked, ReadyPaint, FuturePaint, Closed, LayoutPending bool
	Failure                                                 error
	DomainClosed, RetirementPending                         bool
}
type ManualSnapshot struct {
	Application app.PendingState
	Clock       execution.ClockReadiness
	Executor    execution.Snapshot
	Windows     []ManualWindowSnapshot // immutable application registration order.
	Closed      bool
	Failure     error
}
type ManualStepResult struct{ Events, OwnerCallbacks, Frames int }

// Manual owns actual offscreen managed windows. Methods have one dispatch
// owner and refuse concurrency/reentrancy; callbacks may call Application APIs,
// but must not call back into this adapter. Clock and executor remain caller
// owned and are never implicitly advanced/stepped/closed.
type Manual struct {
	self           *Manual
	busy           atomic.Bool
	closed         atomic.Bool
	implementation *manualImplementation
}

# Independent P9 replay consumer candidate

This temporary standalone module declares a real managed UI workload, using only public Vellum app, command, execution, history, tasks, ui and virtual APIs. `vellum/` is an isolated source snapshot of those root-module dependencies, so ongoing canonical/native integration cannot silently change this qualification. No canonical files, native windows, OS preferences or Git state are changed.

The window is 860 x 620 logical units. Open fixture installs the embedded exact JSON as a clean project through history.Replace. The project-name TextField accepts a controlled UTF-8 edit through history.Apply; Undo/Redo share the Registry, toolbar and native shortcuts. A virtual.Table projects eight immutable keyed rows into four keyed pooled public row buttons in a Scroll; Sort names produces Alpha/Beta/Delta/Eta in the first viewport. A Manual-injected task captures immutable row data and revision, computes checksum42, and uses bounded reserved owner completion. Cancel before stepping still runs worker cleanup and produces one canceled owner result; an edit before an uncanceled result makes it stale.

The View also declares a checkbox that disables the field, a property remount command, and a modal. Background nodes stay enabled while the modal is open so a native test must demonstrate actual modal interception; Registry independently rejects a bypass. UIAttempts counts actual declared Change/Activate callbacks, so a broken router cannot hide behind model-level refusal. The portable qualification never invokes those callbacks. PropertyIncarnation is the consumer's declared remount counter; the live adapter must independently validate its actual mounted record incarnation before routing.

`New(Config{Owner, Executor, Window})` requires an explicit executor, registers one public app.Window, and returns the fixture's Owner/Window/Commands/Journal/Table. Configure before Run; then Invoke/View/Validate/Snapshot are owner-only. `Invoke(ctx, Action)` is a command-only input with checked payload/context/availability and optional history-revision guard. `View` is the exact descriptor for the actual adapter; native input must use hit testing/focus/key dispatch to invoke callbacks. Snapshot deep-copies model/result data, declared semantic child order, minimum/grow constraints and viewport. It explicitly does not contain native focus, measured glyph/layout rectangles, composed pixels or OS accessibility.

## Portable evidence

Run `go run ./cmd/portable -batch 7` with a writable GOCACHE. RunCommands queues open/edit/sort/select/start/cancel/undo on public PostWindow, drains with DrainN, explicitly steps one Manual job, and drains the reserved result. Batches1/7/64 produce identical checkpoints/final model and declared semantics. Final property is North Star, history clean with one redo, sorted visible IDs r-alpha/r-beta/r-delta/r-eta, selected r-alpha, one canceled result and one worker cleanup. Executor and owner mailbox are terminal, while DirtyWindows remains1: a render/reconciliation is still required and no UI quiescence is claimed.

Qualification includes race20/vet/build and exact-source/binary JSON outputs at acceptance/qualification.json. Tests exercise disabled/modal/stale revision and invalid payload refusal, remount/history retention, detached snapshots, full ordinary queue result admission, canceled/window-closed accepted cleanup and refused executor refunds. These command-only tests do not qualify real UI routing. The native consumer must append actual post-frame semantic/focus/layout/image captures and replay actual pointer/key records across the same batches with pinned fonts/theme/viewport/time, refusing disabled/modal/stale/closed mounted targets.
